title.purpose: Page headings (New run, Models). Only use above 14px.

label.purpose: Form labels, section headers, button text, tab labels. The primary text size for all chrome.

mono-data.purpose: All machine-generated values: run IDs, costs, steps, elapsed, tool names, model identifiers, diff lines.

mono-xs.purpose: Secondary metadata in constrained spaces: timestamps, step numbers, kbd hints.

shadows.name: follow-anchor
shadows.purpose: Elevates the ↓ Follow anchor button above the live feed scroll container. Only appears when auto-scroll is paused. The only shadow in the build.

motion.name: pulse-running
motion.purpose: Status dot pulse on created / in-progress / awaiting runs. Signals the run is consuming the developer's attention now.

motion.name: streaming-cursor
motion.purpose: ▋ cursor glyph on .streaming-cursor::after in amber-400. Signals live text is arriving.

motion.name: loading-spinner
motion.purpose: Loader2 icon on find-search and start-run loading states only. Not used for data loading or navigation.

motion.name: hover-transition
motion.purpose: All interactive elements. Tailwind transition-colors default. No explicit duration override in the codebase.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: Start run. Full-width on form pages. Amber on near-black.

components.name: Secondary Button
components.description: Find issues, secondary actions. Dark surface with light text.
components.css: .ds-btn-secondary { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; padding: 8px 16px; background-color: #27272a; color: #e4e4e7; font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 14px; font-weight: 400; border: none; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; transition: background-color 150ms ease-in-out; } .ds-btn-secondary:hover { background-color: #3f3f46; } .ds-btn-secondary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #f59e0b; outline-offset: 2px; } .ds-btn-secondary:disabled { opacity: 0.4; cursor: not-allowed; }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Sidebar nav, collapse toggles. No background at rest.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 4px; padding: 4px 8px; background-color: transparent; color: #71717a; font-family: 'Inter', system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 400; border: none; border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; transition: color 150ms ease-in-out, background-color 150ms ease-in-out; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color: #d4d4d8; background-color: #27272a; } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid #f59e0b; outline-offset: 2px; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: GitHub URL, repo path, issue file, search prompt. Focus shifts border to amber.
components.css: .ds-input { width: 100%; padding: 8px 12px; background-color: #18181b; border: 1px solid #27272a; border-radius: 4px; color: #f4f4f5; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 14px; outline: none; transition: border-color 150ms ease-in-out; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #52525b; } .ds-input:focus { border-color: rgba(245, 158, 11, 0.5); }

components.name: Status Chip
components.description: Inline run status indicator with dot. Dot pulses on active runs.
components.css: .ds-status-chip { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 6px; font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', ui-monospace, monospace; font-size: 12px; } .ds-status-dot { display: inline-block; width: 6px; height: 6px; border-radius: 50%; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-status-running { color: #f59e0b; } .ds-status-running .ds-status-dot { background-color: #f59e0b; animation: ds-pulse-amber 1.5s ease-in-out infinite; } .ds-status-submitted { color: #10b981; } .ds-status-submitted .ds-status-dot { background-color: #10b981; } .ds-status-failed { color: #ef4444; } .ds-status-failed .ds-status-dot { background-color: #ef4444; } .ds-status-cancelled { color: #71717a; } .ds-status-cancelled .ds-status-dot { background-color: #52525b; } @keyframes ds-pulse-amber { 0%, 100% { opacity: 1; } 50% { opacity: 0.4; } }

components.name: Tool Call Card
components.description: Expandable card for each tool call in the live feed. Amber tool name, chevron toggle.
components.css: .ds-tool-card { border: 1px solid #27272a; border-radius: 4px; background-color: rgba(24,24,27,0.6); overflow: hidden; } .ds-tool-card-header { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; width: 100%; padding: 8px 12px; background: none; border: none; cursor: pointer; text-align: left; transition: background-color 150ms ease-in-out; } .ds-tool-card-header:hover { background-color: rgba(39,39,42,0.4); } .ds-chevron { color: #71717a; flex-shrink: 0; } .ds-tool-step { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 10px; color: #71717a; } .ds-tool-name { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; font-weight: 500; color: #fbbf24; } .ds-tool-preview { font-family: 'JetBrains Mono', monospace; font-size: 12px; color: #71717a; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap; }

components.description: Radio card for choosing how to start a run. Selected state uses amber-500/5 tint + amber border.

narrative.overview:
Iaso's UI is not a chat window and not a summary dashboard. It is a reviewer's console — a surface designed for the act of watching an agent work and judging its output with the same rigor you would apply to a code review. Every design decision defers to that job: the developer is a reviewer, not a prompt author, and the UI earns no attention it does not need.

The world is near-black (zinc-950, #09090b). Surfaces are zinc-900 (#18181b). There is no decorative color: amber is

Color works exactly like a terminal's status output, and nothing else.

Density is the value proposition. This UI is opened in a split-attention state — editor in one window, browser tab in another — so it must surface maximum information in minimum space. Labels are text-xs (12px). Metadata is text-[10px] (10px) in monospace. There is no body prose on any screen except the report tab.
keyCharacteristics: Near-black background; zinc-900 surfaces; zinc-800 borders — a strict three-layer tonal stack
Amber is the single accent; it appears only on active/awaiting state, focus rings, selected rows, and the primary CTA
Monospace (JetBrains Mono) for all data — run IDs, costs, steps, elapsed times, tool names, diff lines
No decorative shadows, no gradients, no glass
Motion is limited to three named uses: status pulse on active runs, streaming cursor on live text, spinner on loading actions

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Amber (#f59e0b) is used in exactly one semantic category per screen: state that requires the developer's attention or the primary action available. It is never used decoratively, never used for category labels, never used to highlight completed or neutral content.

rules.name: The Cancelled Rule
rules.body: Cancelled is not an error. Its dot is zinc-600 (#52525b), not zinc-500; its label text is zinc-500 (#71717a). The distinction between cancelled and muted metadata is intentional and must be preserved.

rules.name: The No-Body Rule
rules.body: This is a tool, not a document. Inter is never used for prose paragraphs on tool screens. The report tab renders agent-generated markdown via Tailwind Typography (prose-sm prose-invert) — this is an isolated rendering context for external content, not part of the design system's type hierarchy.

rules.name: The Mono-Data Rule
rules.body: Every value that could appear in a terminal — run IDs, costs, steps, model identifiers, tool call names, diff lines, file paths — uses JetBrains Mono. Inter is reserved for human-authored labels and instructions.

rules.name: The Tonal Stack Rule
rules.body: Surfaces at different depths are expressed only through the zinc ramp: near-black background, dark surface, border. No drop shadows create this layering.

rules.name: The One Radius Rule
rules.body: The build uses one border-radius value everywhere: 4px (Tailwind rounded). No mixed-radius treatment. Rounded pills (rounded-full) appear only on the 6×6px status dots.

dos: Do use zinc-800 (#27272a) borders at 1px for all card, panel, and divider separations.
Do use JetBrains Mono for every value a developer might see in a terminal.
Do show the pulsing amber dot (pulse-running, 1.5s ease-in-out) on status chips for created, in-progress, and awaiting states only.
Do use amber (#f59e0b) on the primary CTA, the approval banner context, focus rings, and the selected sidebar row's left border.
Do use text-zinc-500 font-mono at text-[10px] for all secondary run metadata in constrained spaces.
donts: Don't add decorative gradients, glass effects, or drop shadows to panels, sidebars, or cards.
Don't use amber on a completed or static state.
Don't introduce a border-radius other than 4px.
Don't use Inter for terminal-style data values (costs, run IDs, step counts).
Don't canonize window.confirm as the design system's confirmation pattern.
